LESSON: LINEAR EQUATIONS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Algebra 2.1 Algebraic Expressions (6 Lessons) Factorizing, simplifying and evalu
Topic 2.2: Linear Equations
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 7

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Linear Equations, part of Algebra 2.1 Algebraic Expressions (6 Lessons) Factorizing, simplifying and evalu in Grade 8 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we solve linear equations in two unknowns? 2. Where do we use linear equations in two unknowns in real-life situations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. form linear equations in two unknowns in real-life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Linear Equations in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. solve linear equations in two unknowns by substitution method in real-life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Linear Equations in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. solve linear equations in two unknowns by elimination method in real-life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Linear Equations in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. apply linear equations in two unknowns in real-life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Linear Equations in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. recognise use of linear equations in real life.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Linear Equations in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. form linear equations in two unknowns in real-life situations,

   Linear Equations helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. solve linear equations in two unknowns by substitution method in real-life situations,

   Linear Equations helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. solve linear equations in two unknowns by elimination method in real-life situations,

   Linear Equations helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. apply linear equations in two unknowns in real-life situations,

   Linear Equations helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. recognise use of linear equations in real life.

   Linear Equations helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. role-play activities such as shopping on two different items in the shop to form linear equations in two unknowns,

2. discuss with others and use activities involving two unknowns,

3. discuss and use substitution method to find the solutions of simultaneous equations in two unknowns,

4. discuss and use elimination method to find the solutions of simultaneous equations in two unknowns,

5. practice forming and solving simultaneous equations in two unknowns of real-life cases using any method, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. role-play activities such as shopping on two different items in the shop to form linear equations in two unknowns,
2. discuss with others and use activities involving two unknowns,
3. discuss and use substitution method to find the solutions of simultaneous equations in two unknowns,
4. discuss and use elimination method to find the solutions of simultaneous equations in two unknowns,
5. practice forming and solving simultaneous equations in two unknowns of real-life cases using any method, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Linear Equations together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.
